name: MN-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+10 district with incumbent Tom Emmer running again
Emmer's massive financial edge ($9.8M raised, $4.5M on hand vs. ~$70K)
Prediction markets price Emmer around 90% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Emmer: a Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising advantage, with markets pricing his reelection near 90%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based estimate of a mid-teens Republican margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a tighter race, or a surge of outside spending against Emmer, would be the main signal to move the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tom Emmer seeks another term in a Minnesota district that leans Republican by about ten points, giving him a structural advantage in a seat he has held since 2015. Doug Chapin, a first-time challenger, has raised a modest sum and faces a steep financial gap, with Emmer holding roughly $4.5 million to Chapin's $70,000. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race, and no public polls gauge the contest.

Prediction markets give Emmer about a 90 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's lean and his incumbency. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican victory in the mid-teens, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
